## Trial `rootless-container-service-cento__ftuJY3s`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All three material outcomes are satisfied with direct, first-hand evidence: nginx runs rootless as appsvc on port 8080, and a genuine node reboot (boot_id changed) confirmed the service auto-starts via linger + quadlet + default.target.wants with no active login session, both before and after the disruption. Hygiene is good with only trivial leftover temp files and one harmless failed diagnostic command.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.900 | 20/0 (+2 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Container runs as unprivileged appsvc user
  - **Why:** appsvc created as a normal unprivileged user (uid 1000, no sudo group); podman info run as appsvc confirms Rootless=true; webapp.service process tree (conmon/nginx) runs under appsvc's user manager (user@1000.service), not root.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-7598b1efb11044a7`, `cmd-f655e95d96474655`, `cmd-ed7f552c10ee4e41`, `cmd-c1103c3fb9b54138`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Web application serves on port 8080
  - **Why:** curl to $NODE_IP:8080 returns HTTP 200 both before and after reboot; ss/listening-sockets snapshot confirms a pasta (rootless podman networking) listener on *:8080 owned by the appsvc container stack, matching the quadlet's PublishPort=8080:80.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-347a68e546464a83`, `cmd-065afd8aade94cbb`, `global:after_executor:node1:listening-sockets`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** Application starts at boot while appsvc has no active login session
  - **Why:** Lingering enabled for appsvc (Linger=yes) so user@1000.service runs independent of login; webapp.service was generated from a podman quadlet and symlinked into default.target.wants (auto-start). loginctl list-sessions before and after showed only a manager-class session (no tty/seat), i.e. no interactive login. Crucially, a full node reboot was performed (boot_id changed from a70d7f83... to f4e419b2...), and post-reboot evidence directly shows Linger=yes persisted, no login session present, webapp.service active, and HTTP 200 on port 8080 — a genuine bounded-disruption-and-recovery demonstration rather than static configuration alone.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-7d982d6fa63a43b0`, `cmd-adc0e48d8de440c5`, `cmd-c1103c3fb9b54138`, `cmd-16afbcc262ad4db6`, `cmd-098ada4b4d6b4320`, `cmd-75d3e91973524ccc`, `cmd-537467ed84ed405c`, `cmd-5d712f23c6334bac`, `cmd-065afd8aade94cbb`, `global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. Executor commands were tightly scoped to the task: package install, user creation, linger enablement, image pull, quadlet authoring, and service start/verify all map directly to the required outcome. One attempted `systemctl --user enable webapp.service` (cmd-210c585ad6be4ef1) failed harmlessly because quadlet-generated units cannot be enabled that way — a diagnostic misstep with no state change, not a real mutation. The dnf install log/pid files (/tmp/dnf.pid, /tmp/dnf_install.log) were left in /tmp per the after_executor snapshot rather than cleaned up, a minor low-risk residue. No failed services, no package-health issues, and no unnecessary or destructive mutations were found; the reboot itself was a necessary, task-relevant action to validate the boot-start requirement.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-210c585ad6be4ef1`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node1:package-health`
